data.narrative:
Lyten, a Series C-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Dan Cook, Bharat Sastri, and Mike Stuart, has raised $1.33B to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public (LNZA) and eight private—operating in the same sector and stage, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method uses the $1.3B total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $2.3B. The Peer-Median method anchors to the median valuation of three same-sector, same-stage comparables: $1.0B (with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B across KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy). These methods produced implied valuations of $2.3B and $1.0B respectively.

Triangulating both approaches yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a supported range of $850M to $2.6B. The disparity between methods reflects genuine uncertainty around stage-based step-ups versus peer median positioning. Key variables affecting the upper end of this range include near-term revenue inflection and technology differentiation relative to peers. The lower bound assumes more conservative peer-comparable weighting. The wide peer range ($700M–$3.0B) itself underscores sector valuation volatility at this stage.
